name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Iran orders tighter Hormuz closure 23 Nov
summary: Iran's army orders a tighter Hormuz closure on 23 Nov; Trump says strikes may resume next year if talks fail
state: Iran's army chief ordered on 23 Nov that the Strait of Hormuz be closed further day by day until Iran's conditions are met, while Qatar's prime minister met Rubio and Vance in Washington to revive talks (Euronews). Iran struck an industrial site in Bahrain on 21 Nov, and Trump said on 22 Nov that strikes on Iran could resume next year if talks fail (Bloomberg via News Tribune). On 23 Nov Iran's UN envoy accused Bahrain of letting US forces use its territory and demanded reparations (Iran International). Attacks on Gulf states and shipping keep the Alert.
for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice for Iran, Bahrain, the UAE and other Gulf states, which can change at short notice. Oil and gas prices stay exposed to further attacks on shipping or energy sites.
rubric_hit: Alert: active state-on-state attacks; Iran struck Bahrain 21 Nov and ships were attacked near Hormuz 23 Nov

sources.title: News Tribune (Bloomberg) — Trump suggests Iran strikes will resume next year

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
